Read-only figure review of the residual-history figure for run r-20261105T174420294303-bank-solve-breakpoint, judged from the rendered PNG attached to this review (image-0.png, 1399x720). No SVG was opened.

What the picture shows. Base (grey, dashed, circular markers) starts at 1.9e-7 at restart update 0, holds flat to update 1, decays to about 7e-8 by update 4, steps down at update 5 to 3e-10, then settles at 1.8e-10 by update 8 - still above the dotted acceptance limit at 1e-10. Head (blue, solid) starts at 1.6e-9 at update 0 and reaches 4.66e-11 at update 1, one decade below the limit. The figure makes the run's conclusion visible without reference to the text: the base arm fails to reach the acceptance limit in eight restarts and the head arm passes on its first.

Caption. The fragment caption (bank-solve-breakpoint.html, figure bank-solve-breakpoint-history) is substantive rather than a title repeat: it names lane 0 of the unchanged sixteen-lane CPU cycle test on sirius, states that each arm restarts after its own two production updates, and quotes the two terminal values, 1.836692e-10 for base after eight updates and 4.662581e-11 for head after one. Both figures agree with the plotted points. No caption finding.

Attachment integrity. The attached PNG is 1399x720 against 1400x720 for the producer's own render at resumed/residual-history.png; the two differ only by sub-pixel resampling along glyph and line edges (5098 of about 1.0 million pixels differ by more than 60 levels, dark-pixel count 8234 against 8785). This is an attachment artefact, not a figure defect, and is recorded so a later reader knows the verdict was formed on a resampled copy of the same drawing rather than on a different render.

No blocking or non-blocking findings: every rubric item was checked against the rendered image and passed.

rubric_verdicts.contrast: pass - near-black axis and tick text on white, head in a saturated blue, base in mid grey (#929292) that stays visible against the white without competing with the head series; the dotted acceptance limit reads as a threshold rather than as a third result.
rubric_verdicts.data_ink: pass - two data series (nine base points, two head points) and one threshold line carry the whole panel; no fills, no shading, no data-free furniture beyond axis ticks and a three-entry legend.
rubric_verdicts.decoration: pass - no gridlines, no gradient, no background fill; top and right spines are absent; the legend is frameless and sits above the panel in clear space.
rubric_verdicts.label_collision: pass - no text is clipped by the canvas edge and no two labels overlap: the legend's three entries are separated, axis labels sit in the outer margins, the y-axis label is rotated in the left margin, and no label is drawn over the data. The head arm's terminal marker at 4.66e-11 sits above the bottom spine with clearance.
rubric_verdicts.legibility: pass - logarithmic y-axis with decade ticks 1e-10 to 1e-7, 9 integer x ticks, both axis labels ('Restart update', 'Fresh residual') and every marker read at a glance; the base and head arms are distinguishable by colour, dash and marker, not by subtlety.
rubric_verdicts.table_form: pass - the content is a per-update convergence history (log-scale decay of two arms against a threshold), a relationship that is naturally a line plot and would lose its shape as a table.
